chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Umar al-A'ajamy, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Umar! Nine-tenths of the Religion is in dissimulation (Taqiyya), and there is no Religion for the one who does not practice dissimulation; and the dissimulation is regarding everything except regarding Al-Nabeez (an intoxicating drink) and the wiping upon the two socks (during ablution)'.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or concealment of faith for protection
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A specific type of intoxicating drink mentioned as an exception
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ: Wiping over the two socks during ritual ablution

ai.seo_question: What are the exceptions to the rule of Taqiyya in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Taqiyya (dissimulation) to the status of 'nine-tenths of the Religion,' emphasizing its centrality to Shia identity and survival under persecution. While generally applicable to all religious acts, the Imam explicitly excludes the consumption of Al-Nabeez and the ritual wiping over the socks (Mas'h) from this rule, indicating that these specific practices must be performed openly regardless of danger. This distinction highlights the balance between preserving life and maintaining core ritual obligations in Shia jurisprudence.
